hypothesis: Additional full CPU passes over only the screening trace may lower frozen BF16 bit-predictor cost beyond the selected one-pass model, without changing architecture or coder runtime.
training: Start from the previous selected one-pass FP32 checkpoint. Repeat the complete screen trace through the unchanged public trainer; each invocation reloads weights and resets Adam moments. No shuffling or holdout training. Save FP32 after each pass and export frozen BF16 at declared checkpoints.
selection: Evaluate all four declared BF16 checkpoints on screen. Select the lowest frozen screen cost; ties prefer fewer passes. Save the selected model hash before any holdout evaluation. Require >=1.0 byte gain against the prior one-pass BF16 on both screen and holdout; do not switch after holdout failure.
acceptance: All four checkpoints, intermediate FP32 weights, logs and failed outcomes retained
Only a both-fixture probability-cost survivor may proceed to a real archive comparison
Do not claim payload or prize gain from replay cost alone
limitations: Both fixtures have appeared in previous research and upstream model was trained on target corpus
Repeated passes on a small trace can overfit; a disjoint fixture is only a limited check
Each pass resets optimizer moments, so this is not continuous multi-epoch Adam
The full-stream online-learning threshold and package size are not evaluated here
